All field notes

These notes come from a season of low tides on one stretch of rocky shore. Each entry records a single pool on a single day: what lived there, how warm the water was, and anything that had changed since the last visit. They are short on purpose, written on the rocks before the tide came back.

Read them in any order. The pools are numbered from the top of the shore down, so the low numbers are the hardy, sun-baked basins that only the highest tides reach, and the high numbers are the crowded pools near the water line, where something new turns up on almost every visit.
